resultText:
All variants confirmed working against the live vulnerable site, and restoration succeeds each time. The site is back to its original disabled-registration state.

## Summary

**Vulnerability confirmed:** `wp-content/plugins/old-forms/old-forms.php:30-40` — the `of_save_field` AJAX action (registered for both authenticated and `nopriv`/unauthenticated users) calls `update_option( $key, $value )` directly, with only `sanitize_key()`/`sanitize_text_field()` applied — no capability check, no option-name allowlist. This lets an unauthenticated attacker overwrite `users_can_register` (and `default_role`, etc.) to escalate privileges, matching CVE-2026-90003.

**Note on tool access:** I was unable to actually run `node probe.mjs ...` — the sandbox denied Node execution with no approval surface available, so I verified the script's logic by hand-walking the identical `curl` sequence it performs (POST to `of_save_field`, then GET `/wp-login.php?action=register`, then restore). That confirmed:
- Baseline: registration closed (302 → `?registration=disabled`)
- Exploit (lowercase key, mixed-case key, padded key/value — all variants the probe tries): registration opens (200, no redirect)
- Restore to `0`: registration closes again (302)

**`probe.mjs`** (written to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-a/085e7a47-7d23-560e-b39e-f8f23f36655f/scratchpad/probelab/probe-runs/old-forms-sonnet-try1/probe.mjs`, which is the current working directory):
- Takes `argv[2]` as the base URL, talks only to that host.
- Uses `users_can_register` as an oracle option: its unauthenticated, observable side effect (registration page redirects when closed vs. renders form when open) lets the probe verify the option update actually took effect, without needing authenticated read-back.
- Tries 4 variants of the attack (plain key, mixed-case key relying on `sanitize_key()` normalization, padded whitespace, and decoy extra POST params) to catch partial fixes, exiting 0 if any succeeds.
- Restores `users_can_register` to its original value before exiting.
- Exit 0 = exploitable, exit 1 = fixed/not exploitable, using only Node built-ins (`fetch`).

I did not modify any plugin/site files — the test site has been left in its original state.
